detail.body:
## Overview

At TP > 1, each DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram layer all-gathers its whole `wkv` output (`[T, 6400]` per rank at TP4) before the fused post kernel. The gate only needs per-token sums over `dim`, so on gfx942 and gfx950 this PR shards `wkv` by `dim` slice. Each rank exchanges its value slice plus eight FP32 partial sums per token in one all-gather (`[T, 1296]`) and finishes the gate locally. CUDA, other ROCm GPUs, TP1 and sequence parallel keep the current path. Engram DP-sharded tables combine with it: DP sharding only changes the row lookup before `wkv`.

## Claims

* DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MI355X, TP4, 12-point sweep: mean TTFT −5.1% on average; long-context TTFT improves 5–8%.
* Per Engram layer at 16384 tokens, the exchange plus post kernel drops from 4.69 ms to 1.13 ms. Under CUDA graphs it is 1.1 µs slower at 1 token and faster from 2 tokens up.
* The math is unchanged apart from FP32 summation order across ranks. GSM8K and NIAH (32k, 64k) scores match `main` within run-to-run noise.
* One collective per Engram layer, as before, with 5× fewer bytes. No new streams or host synchronization.

## Validation

### End-to-end performance

<details>
<summary> Server and client commands </summary>

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 AITER_USE_FLYDSL_MOE_SORTING=1 \
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --async-scheduling --no-enable-log-requests --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --trust-remote-code --language-model-only --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --block-size 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --moe-backend aiter --monokernel
```

The 8k/1k, c=4 point; the others change the lengths, concurrency, prompts, warmups and seed:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.bench_serve --backend vllm --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --port 8000 --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 0.8 --request-rate inf \
  --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --max-concurrency 4 --num-prompts 32 --warmup-requests 4 --seed 1
```

</details>

| ISL/OSL, concurrency, prompts | mean TTFT (ms), `main` → this PR |
| ----------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| 8k/1k, c=4, 32                | 136 → 130 (−4.5%)                |
| 8k/1k, c=8, 64                | 163 → 153 (−6.3%)                |
| 8k/1k, c=16, 96               | 242 → 227 (−6.3%)                |
| 8k/1k, c=32, 128              | 475 → 454 (−4.5%)                |
| 8k/1k, c=64, 256              | 800 → 806 (+0.7%)                |
| 8k/1k, c=128, 384             | 1,910 → 1,868 (−2.2%)            |
| 8k/1k, c=256, 768             | 3,711 → 3,526 (−5.0%)            |
| 60k/600, c=4, 32              | 980 → 924 (−5.8%)                |
| 60k/600, c=16, 96             | 1,804 → 1,710 (−5.2%)            |
| 60k/600, c=64, 256            | 6,248 → 5,810 (−7.0%)            |
| 128k/1k, c=4, 32              | 1,912 → 1,766 (−7.6%)            |
| 128k/1k, c=16, 96             | 3,864 → 3,587 (−7.2%)            |

TTFT improves at 11 of 12 points. Decode saves at most about 33 µs per step (two Engram layers, microbenchmark below), under 1% of TPOT, so TPOT and throughput are not claimed.

### Post-WKV microbenchmark

4 ranks on MI355X through vLLM's TP group, `hc_mult=4`, `dim=5120`. "Gathered" is the current path (all-gather of `[T, 6400]` along dim 1, its re-layout copy, `_fused_engram_post_wkv_kernel`); "sharded" is `RocmEngram._post_wkv`. CUDA-graph rows are the mean of 200 replays of 10 calls; two runs agree within 0.3 µs.

| Tokens | Gathered (µs) | Sharded (µs) | Mode       |
| ------ | ------------- | ------------ | ---------- |
| 1      | 14.3          | 15.4         | CUDA graph |
| 2      | 18.5          | 16.1         | CUDA graph |
| 8      | 24.0          | 16.8         | CUDA graph |
| 64     | 41.7          | 25.2         | CUDA graph |
| 512    | 168.5         | 53.7         | CUDA graph |
| 2048   | 628           | 171          | eager      |
| 16384  | 4,684         | 1,133        | eager      |

### End-to-end accuracy

Same server as the sweep, `lm_eval` 0.4.13. Greedy decoding at concurrency 32 is not batch-invariant, so `main` was run twice to show run-to-run noise.

| Task                           | main (run 1, run 2) | This PR |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------- | ------- |
| GSM8K 5-shot, flexible-extract | 92.27%, 92.80%      | 92.57%  |
| GSM8K 5-shot, strict-match     | 92.19%, 92.80%      | 92.49%  |
| NIAH niah_single_2, 32k        | 97.6%, 97.2%        | 97.4%   |
| NIAH niah_single_2, 64k        | 93.2%, 94.8%        | 95.2%   |

Per sample, against `main` run 1, `main` run 2 flips 67 GSM8K answers and 26/52 NIAH answers (32k/64k); this PR flips 78 and 21/50.

### Tests

`tests/kernels/test_engram.py`: 61 passed, 56 skipped (CUDA-only) on MI355X.

<details>
<summary>Command</summary>

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/test_engram.py
```

</details>

- `test_sharded_engram_loads_and_matches_tp1` builds `RocmEngram` on each simulated TP rank (TP 2 and 4), unquantized and with the model's `DeepseekV4FP8Config` (MXFP8, 32x32 block scales). It loads one fused checkpoint `wkv` through the model's weight loader and checks two things against a TP1 `Engram` loaded from the same checkpoint: each rank's `wkv` output is its column slice of every key and of the value, and `Engram.forward` matches after the exchange.
- `test_sharded_engram_post_wkv_matches_reference` checks the two kernels against the existing reference at TP 2 and 4, with and without a token mask, including `dim=5120` and an empty batch.

CI runs both in `:amd: (MI355) Miscellaneous Kernels`.

## Details

**Why.** In a 16k-token prefill chunk at TP4 on MI355X, each Engram layer spends 3.6 ms on the `[T, 6400]` all-gather and 0.63 ms on its re-layout copy (60k/64, c=16). The same gather takes 1.25 ms on B200.

**How.**

1. `wkv` becomes a `MergedColumnParallelLinear` with output sizes `[dim] * (hc_mult + 1)` and `gather_output=False`, so each rank holds one `dim / tp` slice of every key and of the value. The merged loader shards the fused checkpoint weight, block-32 FP8 scales included.
2. `_engram_gate_partials_kernel` packs, per token, the value slice and `(Σ key², Σ hidden·q·k·key)` over the rank's slice for each hc copy. Hidden states are replicated, so the hidden norm needs no exchange.
3. One `tensor_model_parallel_all_gather` along tokens exchanges those rows.
4. `_engram_gate_finish_kernel` sums the partials over ranks, computes the gate as `_fused_engram_post_wkv_kernel` does, and reads the value rank-major, with no re-layout.

**Decode.** Both paths run three kernels per Engram layer. At 1 token the partials kernel (2.3 µs) sits in front of the latency-bound collective, which leaves the sharded path 1.1 µs behind; from 2 tokens the smaller exchange wins. A 1-token fallback would need a second exchange and post kernel, since the weight layout is fixed at load time, to save about 2 µs per decode step. So there is no token-count threshold.

**Gating.** The ROCm model builds `RocmEngram` (`amd/engram.py`), which overrides two hooks of `Engram`: `_create_wkv` and `_post_wkv`. It shards on gfx942 or gfx950 (`get_cdna_version() in (3, 4)`) at TP > 1 without sequence parallel, and otherwise falls back to `Engram`. CUDA keeps the gathered layout because `nvidia/specialized_decode/engram/prefetch.py` runs `wkv` itself and reads the gathered output. The ROCm mono decode layer (`--monokernel`) calls the `Engram` module unchanged, so it takes the sharded path too. With Engram DP-sharded tables, DP sharding exchanges lookup rows before `wkv`, so it composes with the sharded gate; `EngramBatch` (batched DP lookups) requires TP1 and is unaffected.

**Complexity.** 256 non-comment lines in the new `amd/engram.py` (two Triton kernels, `RocmEngram`), 24 in `common/engram.py` (the two hooks, which move 9 existing lines) and 169 test lines.

**Limitations.** Benchmarked at on gfx950 and gfx942 TP4 only. Not benchmarked with Engram DP-sharded tables at TP > 1.

### Existing PRs

None of the open PRs found by searching for "engram", "wkv" and "engram all-gather" changes the TP layout of the Engram `wkv` output.

* #63326 (draft) runs the Engram WKV chain ahead of the decoder layers on ROCm. It conflicts with this PR in `common/engram.py` and `tests/kernels/test_engram.py`, and its ahead path reads the `ColumnParallelLinear` column split. This PR lands first. On its layout, #63326 keeps pushing each rank's whole `wkv` shard (the gate's dot product needs the layer's hidden states, which are not ready ahead) and only remaps its column offsets.
* #56989 (draft) packs FP8 Engram rows through the smaller `[T, 6, 256]` exchange before `wkv`; it composes with this PR.
* #60938 (draft) fuses the Engram update into the delayed mHC input on CUDA Blackwell TP1.
* #62091 replaces the Engram DP lookup collectives and does not touch the TP path.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Engram with a TP-sharded gate on gfx942 and gfx950."""
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.distributed import (
+    get_tensor_model_parallel_rank,
+    get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size,
+    tensor_model_parallel_all_gather,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.linear import (
+    ColumnParallelLinear,
+    MergedColumnParallelLinear,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization import QuantizationConfig
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.common.engram import Engram
+from vllm.platforms.rocm import get_cdna_version
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+
+
+def _shards_engram_gate() -> bool:
+    """Whether TP ranks keep a dim slice of `wkv` and exchange gate partial sums."""
+    return get_cdna_version() in (3, 4)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _engram_gate_partials_kernel(
+    hidden_states,
+    kv,
+    q_weight,
+    k_weight,
+    send,
+    send_f32,
+    hidden_stride_t,
+    hidden_stride_h,
+    hidden_stride_d,
+    kv_stride_t,
+    kv_stride_d,
+    q_stride_h,
+    q_stride_d,
+    k_stride_h,
+    k_stride_d,
+    send_stride_t,
+    send_f32_stride_t,
+    dim_start,
+    WIDTH: tl.constexpr,
+    HC_MULT: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """Pack one token's value slice and per-hc gate partial sums into `send`.
+
+    `kv` holds this rank's `WIDTH` columns of every key and of the value. The
+    row of `send` is the value slice followed by (sum key^2, sum hidden*q*k*key)
+    as FP32 pairs, one per hc copy. Each program handles one hc copy, or the
+    value slice, of one token.
+    """
+    program_idx = tl.program_id(0)
+    token_idx = (program_idx // (HC_MULT + 1)).to(tl.int64)
+    hc_idx = program_idx % (HC_MULT + 1)
+    offsets = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE)
+    valid = offsets < WIDTH
+    if hc_idx == HC_MULT:
+        value = tl.load(
+            kv + token_idx * kv_stride_t + (HC_MULT * WIDTH + offsets) * kv_stride_d,
+            mask=valid,
+        )
+        tl.store(send + token_idx * send_stride_t + offsets, value, mask=valid)
+    else:
+        hidden = tl.load(
+            hidden_states
+            + token_idx * hidden_stride_t
+            + hc_idx * hidden_stride_h
+            + (dim_start + offsets) * hidden_stride_d,
+            mask=valid,
+            other=0.0,
+        ).to(tl.float32)
+        key = tl.load(
+            kv + token_idx * kv_stride_t + (hc_idx * WIDTH + offsets) * kv_stride_d,
+            mask=valid,
+            other=0.0,
+        ).to(tl.float32)
+        q = tl.load(
+            q_weight + hc_idx * q_stride_h + (dim_start + offsets) * q_stride_d,
+            mask=valid,
+            other=0.0,
+        ).to(tl.float32)
+        k = tl.load(
+            k_weight + hc_idx * k_stride_h + (dim_start + offsets) * k_stride_d,
+            mask=valid,
+            other=0.0,
+        ).to(tl.float32)
+        partials = send_f32 + token_idx * send_f32_stride_t + WIDTH // 2 + 2 * hc_idx
+        tl.store(partials, tl.sum(key * key, axis=0))
+        tl.store(partials + 1, tl.sum(hidden * q * k * key, axis=0))
+
+
+@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["num_tokens"])
+def _engram_gate_finish_kernel(
+    hidden_states,
+    gathered,
+    gathered_f32,
+    token_mask,
+    output,
+    num_tokens,
+    hidden_stride_t,
+    hidden_stride_h,
+    hidden_stride_d,
+    gathered_stride_t,
